title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X_* is a simplicial set and k a commutative ring. Grothendieck builds a bigraded, divided-power analogue of Sullivan's polynomial de Rham complex. On Δ^n, Sullivan uses k[t_0..t_n]/(Σt_i − 1), which needs Q. The relation Σt_i = 1 is not homogeneous, so Grothendieck homogenizes it to Σ t_i = T, where T is an extra divided-power variable with dT = 0. The forms on Δ^n are then Γ_k(t_0..t_n) ⊗ Λ(dt_i) / (Σt_i = T, Σdt_i = 0) ≅ Γ_k(T, t_1..t_n) ⊗ Λ(dt_1..dt_n), with d(t^{[n]}) = t^{[n−1]}dt. Gluing over simplices gives C^{··}_{DRpd}(X_*,k), a bigraded commutative dga over S = Γ_k(T), with divided powers. The bigrading is PD-polynomial degree and form degree; d has bidegree (−1,+1) and preserves total 'weight'.

Why this works integrally. The PD Poincaré lemma holds over any ring, because ∫ t^{[n]}dt = t^{[n+1]}. Extendability fails in low weight, however. On Δ^1, f(T) − f(0) always lies in the augmentation ideal of Γ(T). So the weight-w piece only sees a truncated version of cohomology. This is the 'théorie des ombres' of the previous page: a graded module or algebra M is recovered from the truncations τ_q(M ⊗_k S) for q large.

A check on S^1 = Δ^1/∂Δ^1, as I compute it: in weight w, H^1 ≅ Z, detected by integration with values in Z·T^{[w]}. Products integrate to T^{[a]}T^{[b]} = C(a+b,a) T^{[a+b]}. So a degree-q class lives at least at T^{[q]}, roughly H^q(X) ⊗ T^{[q]}. This explains how a PD structure can coexist with cup products such as x^p ≠ 0 in H^*(CP^∞; F_p). For |x| = 2 one gets (x T^{[2]})^{[p]} = x^p ⊗ ((2p)!/(p! 2^p)) T^{[2p]}, which is integral. This consistency check is my reconstruction, not on the page.

The page proceeds as follows.
- Top line: it finishes the previous sentence. One hopes C_DRpd also yields RΓ(X_*,k) ∈ D(k) together with the cup product RΓ ⊗^L RΓ → RΓ.
- Remark a): Over a Q-algebra k, Sullivan's complex is recovered as C_DRS(X_*,k) ≅ C_DRpd(X_*,k)/(T−1). For arbitrary k one gets C_DRS(X_*, k⊗Q) ≅ C_DRpd(X_*,k)/(T−1). Rationalization is automatic: T^n = n! T^{[n]}, so T = 1 forces every n! to be a unit. More generally, for a PD triple (S,J,t) with t ∈ J, specializing T ↦ t gives C_DRpd(X_*;S,J,t)/(t−1) ≅ C_DRS(X_*, S_Q/(t−1)).
- Remark b): Grothendieck is 'convinced' that the PD structure on the augmentation ideal of C_DRpd → H^0(X_*,k) (locally constant functions) is important. He poses the question: for X_* simply connected, with finiteness conditions on the H_i(X_*) (marginal addition), does C_DRpd(X_*,k) with all its structure, including the divided powers, determine the homotopy type?
- Next page: this becomes a conjectural equivalence. Simply connected homotopy types with finitely generated H_i(X,Z) would correspond to a localized ('derived') category of PD de Rham complexes over Z, with H^0 = Z, H^1 = 0 and finite-type cohomology. It is an integral analogue of Sullivan–Quillen rational homotopy theory.
errors: H^0(X_*,k) = Hom(X_*,k) is loose: it should be Hom(π_0(X_*),k), i.e. locally constant functions.
Notation drifts between C^{··}_{DRpd} and \mathcal{K}^{··}_{DRpd} for the same object.
In the (S,J,t) formula, S/(t−1) is already a Q-algebra (since t^n = n! t^{[n]}), so writing S_Q/(t−1) is harmless but redundant.

The equivalence suggested on the next page is very optimistic. Strictly commutative cochain models over Z or F_p are known to lose information (Steenrod operations). It is unclear whether the bigraded T-weight plus PD structure compensates. The full-faithfulness/essential-image claim is unproven and may well be false as stated.

ideas.what: Homogenized divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on simplices (Σt_i = T, with T a PD variable), giving a bigraded PD cdga C_DRpd(X_*,k) over Γ_k(T) for any ring k
ideas.modern_name: Integral/divided-power analogue of Sullivan's A_PL; Rees-type homogenization of the simplicial PD de Rham algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) for A_PL; Cartan (Séminaire Cartan 1954–55) for PD algebras; integral and tame variants by Cenkl–Porter and others. I do not know a published source for the homogenized PD version.
ideas.where_published: Only in these 1976 IHÉS conference notes, as far as I know

ideas.what: Recovering Sullivan's rational complex as C_DRpd/(T−1), with rationalization forced automatically by T^n = n! T^{[n]}; base-change version for PD triples (S,J,t)
ideas.modern_name: Specialization of a Rees/filtered object at T = 1; rationalization via divided powers
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; not aware of this exact statement in the literature

ideas.what: 'Shadow theory': a graded k-module or algebra is determined by the truncations τ_q(M ⊗ S) for large q, so the bigraded C_DRpd determines H^*(X,k) with cup product
ideas.modern_name: Recovering a filtered/graded object from its Rees module; weight-truncation bookkeeping

ideas.what: Question/conjecture: C_DRpd(X,Z) with its PD structure determines simply connected finite-type homotopy types, possibly via an equivalence of homotopy categories
ideas.modern_name: Integral homotopy theory via commutative cochain models; Grothendieck's schematization problem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mandell (E∞ cochains over F̄_p, 2001; over Z, 2006); Toën (affine stacks, schematization, 2000s–2020); Ekedahl (minimal models in integral homotopy theory, 2002); Horel (binomial rings and homotopy theory, ~2022)
ideas.where_published: The schematization problem appears in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and the 1975 letters to Breen; the PD de Rham formulation does not, to my knowledge

missed.claim: An explicit integral, divided-power, bigraded version of Sullivan's polynomial forms, obtained by homogenizing the simplex relation to Σt_i = T. Sullivan's complex is recovered exactly as the quotient by (T−1), which automatically tensors with Q. The base-change formula for PD triples (S,J,t) is also stated.
missed.quote: quel que soit k, on a C_DRS(X_*, k⊗_Z Q) ≃ C_DRpd(X_*,k)/(T−1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives one integral object that specializes to the rational Sullivan model at T = 1. Its T-graded pieces carry truncated integral cohomology with divided powers, a Rees-type deformation not standard in the integral homotopy theory literature. The homogenization trick seems to be how the PD structure is made compatible with cup products such as x^p ≠ 0 mod p.

missed.claim: Grothendieck links divided-power (crystalline-style) algebra with the reconstruction of integral homotopy types. He insists that the PD structure on the augmentation ideal over H^0 = functions on π_0 is the key extra structure.
missed.quote: Je suis convaincu que la structure [p.d.], i.e. sur l'idéal d'augmentation ... est importante
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates the modern search for algebraic models of integral homotopy theory: Mandell's E∞ cochains, Toën's affine stacks, and Horel's / Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov's binomial rings, where functions on π_0 form a binomial ring. The PD-bigraded variant does not appear to have been tested against these results.

missed.claim: Precise conjecture: for simply connected X with finite-type homology, C_DRpd(X,Z) with all structures determines the homotopy type, possibly giving an equivalence with a localized category of PD de Rham complexes.
missed.quote: si la connaissance de C_DRpd(X_*,k) avec toutes ses structures (y compris celles de p.d.) [n']implique pas la connaissance du type d'homotopie de X_*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Neither faithfulness nor fullness has been examined for this specific strictly commutative bigraded PD model, to my knowledge. It could be compared with Mandell's 2006 theorem and Horel's binomial full faithfulness.

deep.surprise_reason: The broad aim — algebraic cochain models for integral homotopy types — is well known and was later pursued by Mandell, Toën and Horel. Grothendieck's link to schematization is also documented. What seems genuinely unrecorded is the concrete construction: homogenizing the simplex as Σt_i = T inside divided-power algebras, recovering Sullivan's forms as the quotient by T−1 with automatic rationalization, and the PD-triple base change, all tied to an explicit integral reconstruction conjecture.
transcription_corrections: 'implique pas' should be read as '[n']implique pas' (the negation is elided in Grothendieck's hand).

Line b) likely reads 'Je suis convaincu que la structure [p.d.], i.e. sur l'idéal d'augmentation de ...'; the struck-through phrase before 'l'idée' looks like 'Je viens de penser à [?] ...', followed by 'l'idée de se poser la question'.
The marginal note reads approximately 'avec conditions de finitude sur les H_i(X_*)', inserted after 'simplement connexe'.
The page number at the top is (10); the archive page is 11.
In the (S,J,t) formula the right-hand side is C_DRS(X_*, S_Q/(t−1)), with the 'C' overwritten in the manuscript.
